newsitem.title: TAIWAN: U.S. ex-Vice-President Quayle visits Taiwan.
newsitem.headline: U.S. ex-Vice-President Quayle visits Taiwan.

text.p: Former U.S. Vice-President Dan Quayle arrived in Taipei on Sunday for a bilateral economic forum, in which both sides will try to strengthen economic ties despite a lack of diplomatic relations.
Taiwan's foreign ministry said U.S. senator Frank Murkowski was also scheduled to arrive in Taipei on Sunday for the joint business conference.
The ministry on Friday said Philip Lader, head of the U.S. Small Business Administration, a government official, would arrive in Taipei on December 9 for the conference.
Analysts had said the official's relatively junior status signalled a snub reflecting warming U.S. ties with China.
Despite the presence of U.S. and Taiwan officials, the forum is deemed unofficial because Washington has diplomatic ties only with Beijing, not Taipei.
Quayle, Lader and Murkowski are scheduled to address the conference and meet Taiwan President Lee Teng-hui and other Taiwan officials, the ministry said in statements.

Analysts say that as tensions between the United States and China ease, Washington may begin to limit high-level exchanges with Taiwan, China's diplomatic rival since a civil war split them in 1949. Washington switched ties to Beijing in 1979.
Presidents Bill Clinton and Jiang Zemin agreed in November at the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation forum to hold summits in Washington in 1997 and Beijing in 1998.

Sino-U.S. ties were damaged when Washington allowed Taiwan President Lee Teng-hui to make a private U.S. visit in mid-1995 and reached a nadir as China mounted missile tests and war games in waters near Taiwan in the runup to the island's March presidential election.

The most recent senior U.S. exchange was a September visit by Deputy Treasury Secretary Lawrence Summers, who was the highest-ranking U.S. official to visit since U.S. Transportation Secretary Federico Pena in December 1994.
